title: correlate-spans-with-batched-log-attachments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently emit high-volume per-span JSON logs from language model inference workers which results in duplicated context (prompt tokens, metadata) and poor Loki index cardinality. Correlating these logs with tracing spans is brittle because trace IDs are sometimes split across processes and attachments (large JSON blobs) cannot be efficiently shipped without inflating storage and ingest costs.

Goal: Introduce a lightweight, backward-compatible 'span-attachment' envelope and a batched attachment writer at the sidecar level that: (1) deduplicates identical attachment payloads, (2) ships attachments in configurable batches to the log fabric, and (3) records compact correlation pointers in the span/log entry so dashboards and trace joins can reconstruct full context without duplicating the attachment across every log line.

Why now: Recent customer incidents and cost spikes (Month-on-month Loki storage +28% from inference tenants) demonstrate we need a cost-aware correlation approach that preserves low-latency trace joins and high-cardinality observability without linear storage growth.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace KV cache optimizations for inference runtime (separate project) and does not attempt to redesign the tracing protocol itself (we will extend existing OTLP fields via adapter).
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar component exposes an HTTP/UNIX socket endpoint for workers to post 1..N attachment blobs (JSON or gzip) with a correlation token
Attachment writer batches attachments and creates dedup keys (sha256) before sending to the ingest fabric
Log entries emit a compact envelope: {span_id, trace_id, attach_ref:<sha256[:12]>, attach_batch_id} instead of full JSON payload
Query-by-attachment on Grafana/Trace UI reconstructs full attachment for a span with <300ms median extra latency for a live trace join
End-to-end e2e test that simulates 10k spans/minute with 20% attachments shows storage drop >=40% versus baseline while P95 trace-join latency remains within SLO
Canary rollout plan documented and rollback path verified (fallback to legacy emitter enabled via feature flag)
design_notes: Attachment envelope: versioned (v1), mime-type, compressed-flag, content-sha256, optional small metadata map (max 256 chars)
Sidecar batching: small in-memory ring buffer keyed by tenant+shard. Flush triggers: size (configurable bytes), time (50ms), or count (100 attachments)

Dedup strategy: attachments deduped on sha256; store reference on object store (S3-compatible) via ingest coordinator and emit a compact pointer to Loki/ELK. Short-lived cache for recent ref->object mapping to speed joins.

Backward-compat: if feature-flag off, sidecar continues to emit full payloads. Ingress accepts both legacy and pointer-based envelopes and materializes objects in object store when pointer received from sidecar.
Security: attachments are tenant-scoped. Use tenant-scoped KMS keys to sign references. Sidecar validates worker token (mTLS + JWT) before accepting attachments.
Observability: new metrics: attach_batch_size_bytes, attach_dedupe_rate, attach_store_latency_ms, attach_join_latency_ms. Add tracing spans for batch_write and object_lookup.
Indexing: Loki index only contains pointer fields and low-cardinality tags (service, tenant, env). Full attachments are not indexed to avoid cardinality explosion.
tasks: RFC PR: submit architecture proposal to drive (confluence) and TECH-SIG (linked)
Implement sidecar HTTP endpoint and local batching (Go): accept attachments, compute sha256, place in batch
Implement dedupe cache (LRU) and object uploader to S3-compatible store
Ingress adapter change: accept pointer envelopes and materialize pointers when queried by trace UI
Add metrics and tracing for every step; wire into Console dashboards
E2E load test harness: 10k spans/min with mixture of small/large attachments
Canary rollout: 5% tenants -> 20% -> 100% with health gates (ingest error rate, join latency, storage), implement feature flag toggle
Docs: SDK sidecar API reference and migration guide for customers that run private deployments
Postmortem runbook entry and rollback procedure
comments: 2026-02-11 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after spike indicated ~2.6x duplication for inference worker attachments. Added rough acceptance criteria.
2026-02-18 - Marco Rivera: Implemented prototype sidecar batcher; local benchmark shows 55% storage reduction when dedupe ratio is 6:1. Pushed branch for internal review (PR#298).
2026-02-22 - Lena Chen (Observability): Reviewed metrics plan. Suggested adding attach_join_latency_ms and low-cardinality indexing to avoid alert fatigue. Added to design_notes.

2026-02-28 - QA: Found race condition when two workers submit identical attachment concurrently — dedupe cache returns conflict and both uploads occurred. Added task to serialize dedupe-check+claim via Redis optimistic lock.
2026-03-05 - Security: Confirmed tenant-scoped signing is acceptable; recommended limiting metadata field to 256 chars to avoid secrets leakage in index tags.
2026-03-09 - Marco Rivera: Integrated object uploader with test S3 bucket and instrumented metrics; canary manifest ready. E2E harness running in CI (link above).
2026-03-12 - Product (Drew McAllister): Approved rollout plan; requested canary gating thresholds: ingest error rate <0.5%, attach_join_latency P95 < 500ms, storage cost reduction >=30%.
